slides.title:
The exam that
stops planes.
slides.sub:
Korea's college entrance exam, Nov 19 2026.
Everything Blip runs into is real.

bubbles.text:
Why is the sky
so… quiet?

fact.text: All takeoffs and landings were suspended from 1:05 to 1:40 p.m., during the exam's English listening section.

bubbles.text:
Glasses, please.
We check every pair.

My whole face
is a screen.

fact.text: Proctors checked every pair of glasses for hidden cameras. Only pencils were allowed in exam rooms.

bubbles.text:
Stickers on
every button?
I'm ALL buttons.

fact.text: Test-takers were handed stickers to cover the buttons on their clothes, to block miniature cameras.
Two disaster alerts were sent to nearly every phone, loud even when muted, to find phones that had not been handed in.

slides.caption: And the reward for reporting a cheater…

fact.text: Up to 100 million won (about $75,000) per confirmed case, plus a 10-year exam ban. The reward still needs rules; the ban still needs a law.
fact.src: PM's office via Yonhap (Nov 18); The Korea Herald (Nov 17, 19)

slides.title: What's real (Nov 19)

rows.text: Planes paused 1:05–1:40 p.m. for the English listening section
Glasses checked, buttons stickered, only pencils
Two loud alerts to nearly every phone
Up to ₩100M (~$75,000) reward: rules being written
10-year exam ban: needs a new law

slides.sources: Sources: The Korea Herald / Yonhap (Nov 17, 19), Yonhap Korean edition (Nov 18). Comic scenes are illustrations; facts are in the strips below each panel.
